Index No.: 160000/2024 
 
 
Plaintiff, JUSTIN SAPINI, by his attorneys, STOLZENBERGCORTELLI, LLP, as 
and for his response to Defendants, ANTHONY F. FERRARA and METRO-NORTH 
COMMUTER RAILROAD’s various Discovery Demands, dated December 2, 2024, upon 
information and belief, set forth the following: 
GENERAL RESPONSES AND OBJECTIONS 
 
Each of the Responding Plaintiff’s responses, in addition to any specifically stated 
objections, is subject to and incorporates the following general responses and objections.  The 
assertion of the same, similar, or additional objections, or a partial response to any individual 
request does not waive any of the plaintiff’s general responses and objections. 
1. 
The following responses reflect the current state of the plaintiff’s knowledge, 
understanding and belief respecting matters about which inquiry has been made.  The plaintiff 
expressly reserves his right to supplement or modify these responses with such pertinent 
information as he may hereafter discover or as may be informed by the opinions of experts 
retained by the parties to testify in the trial of this matter and will do so to the extent required 
by the CPLR.  The plaintiff expressly reserves the right to rely on, at any time, including trial, 
subsequently discovered documents and/or materials that have been produced promptly upon 
discovery.

2. 
The plaintiff objects to any demand that seeks information constituting or 
containing information concerning communications between the plaintiff and his counsel, 
which are protected by the attorney-client privilege. 
 
3. 
The plaintiff objects to any demand that seeks information constituting or 
containing information prepared in anticipation of or as a result of litigation or which is 
otherwise protected by the work product doctrine or other available privilege or protection. 
 
4. 
The inadvertent provision of information or the production by the plaintiff of 
documents containing information protected from discovery by the attorney-client privilege, 
work product doctrine or any other applicable privilege, shall not constitute a waiver of such 
privileges with respect to that information or those or any other documents.  In the event that 
inadvertent production occurs, the Defendants shall return all inadvertently produced 
documents to the plaintiff upon request, and/or shall make no use of the contents of such 
information or documents nor premise any further discovery on information learned 
therefrom. 
 
5. 
The plaintiff objects to any demand to the extent that it purports to impose 
upon him/her any obligation beyond those imposed by the CPLR. 
 
6. 
The plaintiff objects to these demands to the extent that they are over-broad, 
unduly burdensome, vague, ambiguous, confusing, require speculation to determine their 
meaning or use imprecise specifications of the information sought. 
 
7. 
The plaintiff objects to any demand to the extent that it seeks information 
neither relevant to the subject matter of this litigation nor reasonably calculated to lead to the 
discovery of admissible evidence.

8. 
The plaintiff objects to any demand as unduly and unnecessarily burdensome 
to the extent that it seeks information that is a matter public record, already in the Defendants’ 
possession, or otherwise readily available to the Defendants, and, therefore, may be accessed 
and obtained by the Defendants with less burden than the plaintiff can identify and provide 
requested information.    
 
9.  
None of the objections or responses contained herein is an admission 
concerning the existence of any documents or materials, the relevance or admissibility of any 
documents, materials or information, or the truth or accuracy of any statement or 
characterization contained in Defendants’ First Set of Discovery Demands. The plaintiff’s 
responses are made without waiving, but, on the contrary, expressly reserving: (a) the right to 
object, on the grounds of competency, privilege, relevancy, materiality or any other proper 
grounds, to the use of the information provided herein, in whole or in part, in any subsequent 
proceeding in this action or any other action; (b) the right to object on any and all grounds, at 
any time, to other discovery requests involving or relating to the subject matter of these 
requests; and (c) the right at any time to revise, correct, add or clarify any of the responses 
provided herein. 
10. 
The plaintiff objects to any demand that seeks information that is already in the 
defendants’ possession. 
 
11. 
Unless otherwise indicated, the plaintiff will not provide information 
encompassed by their general responses and objections or by their specific objections set forth 
below.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIONS AND RESPONSES 
 
 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR WITNESS INFORMATION 
 
 
Plaintiff is not aware of any witnesses to the within accident other than the parties 
named herein and those listed on the Police Accident Report. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR PARTY STATEMENTS  
PURSUANT TO CPLR 3101(E) 
 
 
Plaintiff took no statements, oral, written, visual, photographic or electronically 
recorded, of the Defendants as contemplated by the CPLR.  Plaintiff reserves the right to 
utilize any such statements at the time of trial if and when discovered.  Plaintiff is not in 
possession of any such transcripts of recorded statements taken of or from the parties, agents, 
servants or employees, other than the 50-h transcript which are provided with plaintiff’s 
discovery responses. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR COPIES OF MEDICAL REPORTS 
 
Plaintiff provided names of his medical providers in his Bill of Particulars along with 
HIPAA authorizations.  A copy of same is being provided with plaintiff’s discovery 
responses and will be exchanged with all parties. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR PRIOR AND/OR SUBSEQUENT INJURIES 
 
Not applicable. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR LAWSUITS AND/OR CLAIMS/INCIDENTS 
 
As a result of the within accident, Plaintiff commenced a lawsuit in New York County 
Supreme Court under index number 150940/2024. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEOS, TAPES, ETC. 
 
 
Plaintiff is in possession of twenty-two (22) color copied photographs depicting the 
property damage to the vehicles involved in the within accident and plaintiff’s injuries.  
Plaintiff is not currently in possession of any videos.

RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR EXPERT WITNESS INFORMATION 
 
 
 
RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR DISCOVERY OF EXPERT 
WITNESS INFORMATION – AS TO ALL EXPERTS 
 
Plaintiff objects to this demand to the extent it seeks information beyond the scope 
required by CPLR 3101(d).  Without waiving said objection, Plaintiff has not specifically 
engaged an expert who is expected to testify at a trial of this action and expressly reserves the 
right to do so and to disclose the identity of the same in accordance with the provisions of the 
C.P.L.R.   Plaintiff objects to providing dates of all reports rendered by each such expert as 
well as code sections, as beyond the scope of disclosure required by CPLR 3101(d).  
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Plaintiff expects to call any physician or other health care 
providers whose name appears in any of Plaintiff’s medical records with respect to this case, 
as well as to any physician or health providers who has examined or treated the Plaintiff in 
connection with the injuries claimed to have resulted from the accident which is the subject 
of this action, including, but not limited to, other physicians and other health providers who 
have examined the Plaintiff.  In addition to the foregoing, this Plaintiff intends to call any 
physician or health care providers whose testimony may be necessary to support, refute or 
rebut claims that are hereinafter alleged or arise during the course of trial.  Said physicians 
will be qualified to testify in the action by virtue of being qualified to practice medicine in the 
State of New York and/or another state, having graduated from medical school, having 
become affiliated with various hospitals, having qualified in a medical specialty, having 
Board certification, having been a member of various medical societies and/or associations; 
and having been otherwise qualified to testify as an expert.  Said physicians will also testify 
on the subject of the Plaintiff’s medical condition, including, but not limited to, the nature 
and extent of the Plaintiff’s injuries and disabilities and their causal connection to the 
accident.

Additionally, Plaintiff reserves the right to produce a radiologist qualified in

who will interpret any x-rays, MRIs or cat-scans which may have been performed on the 
Plaintiff in connection with the diagnosis and treatment of the injuries sustained in the 
accident.

RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR LETTERS OR WRITTEN 
COMMUNICATIONS 
 
Not applicable. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR INSURANCE INFORMATION 
 
Not applicable to plaintiff.  This demand is hereby directed to all defendants. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR SOCIAL MEDIA 
 
Plaintiff objects to this demand to the extent that defendants seek social media login 
information and passwords. Plaintiff will however allow defendants to view plaintiff’s social 
media posts - not private conversations - only after plaintiff’s deposition has been completed 
in the presence of plaintiff and his counsel at plaintiff’s counsel's office, if plaintiff has social 
media accounts. 
RESPONSE TO DEMAND FOR STATEMENT OF DAMAGES 
 
Plaintiff objects to this demand as improper as Plaintiff places his trust in a trier of 
fact to determine the total damages to which Plaintiff may be entitled. Over said objection, 
but without waiving same, Plaintiff states that he was damaged in an amount to be 
determined by a trier of fact, not to exceed $10,000,000. 
 
Plaintiff expressly reserves his right to supplement and amend each of the foregoing 
responses up to and including the time of trial.
